name: Pink-breasted Lark
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern ethiopia to kenya, eastern uganda, and northern tanzania
description: An unusual lark with a slim bill and pinkish-brown markings on the face and underparts. Unlike many larks, shows no white in the outer tail or rufous in the wing in flight.

name: Chestnut-bellied Malkoha
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar, southern thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Large, rather ungainly cuckoo; clambers about in the middle and upper levels of lowland forests and edges as it forages. Glossy green above, gray below and on head, with neon-orange skin around the eye, chestnut-orange belly and undertail coverts, greenish-yellow bill, and white-tipped green tail.

name: White-spotted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to southeastern paraguay, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Small, noisy woodpecker, common in a variety of forested habitats including urban parks. The body is largely olive-green and heavily barred, including the tail.

name: Tapajos Antpitta
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil, south of the amazon river, from the right (east) bank of the rio madeira to the upper rio xingu
description: Retiring species, almost tailless with very long robust legs. Has a reddish brown-back and white underparts streaked olive-gray.

name: Taiwan Bamboo-Partridge
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Medium-sized, mostly brownish terrestrial bird with a slate-gray head and neck, dark orange throat, and rusty spots on sides and wings. Endemic to Taiwan., where it inhabits lowland and foothill forests with undergrowth and densely vegetated edges, where difficult to see.

name: Hawaiian Petrel
rangeDescription: Hawaiian islands; ranges southward to polynesia
description: A large, long-winged petrel that appears mostly dark above and white below. The forehead is white and the underwings have a broad black diagonal bar.

name: Henderson Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds henderson island (southeastern pacific); wintering range unknown
description: A typical uniformly grayish-brown petrel with pale mottling at the base of the bill that gives it a somewhat “frosted” facial appearance. Pale bar along the leading edge of the underwing between the body and elbow is evident in flight.
imageCreditName: Fernando Díaz I Albatross Birding Chile

name: Masked Yellowthroat
rangeDescription: Northeastern colombia to venezuela, trinidad, the guianas, and northern brazil
description: Skulking warbler of grassy areas such as overgrown fields and marshes. Male has a striking black bandit mask, and his gray crown helps to separate him from other yellowthroats in range.

name: Screaming Cowbird
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized cowbird found at woodland edges, savannas, and agricultural areas. Both sexes are entirely black with a bluish iridescence, except for rufous feathers on the underwing, which are difficult to see.

name: Speckled Boobook
rangeDescription: Sulawesi, including kabaena, muna, and buton islands (to se)
description: A distinctive medium-sized owl with a rounded head, prominent white eyebrows, dark eyes, a white belly, and a widely spotted gray upperside and crown. Found in forest and edge in the lowlands and foothills, often in pairs.

name: White-winged Guan
rangeDescription: Dry forest of northwestern peru (tumbes, piura and lambayeque)
description: Large, turkey-like bird restricted to dry forests of northwestern Peru. Dark brown overall, with a red wattle, a pink face patch, and white scaling on the breast.

name: Timneh Parrot
rangeDescription: Southern guinea to sierra leone, liberia, mali, and western ivory coast
description: Large gray parrot with a white face and brick red tail. Main habitat is lowland and mid-elevation forest, but will sometimes also use gallery forest, secondary forest, mangroves, and cultivated areas, especially oil palm.

name: Hunter's Cisticola
rangeDescription: High mountains of western kenya, uganda, and northern tanzania
description: A large, plain cisticola with a reddish cap and two bands across the tail tip, one pale and one dark. Found in open montane habitats with thick herbaceous undergrowth, including forest edge, grassland, and heath, almost always in pairs or small groups.

name: White-throated Mountain-Babbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern nigeria and southwestern cameroon
description: A strange, chunky rusty-brown forest babbler with a white face and throat, pale blue-gray eyes, and a pale bill, rendering it unmistakable. Juvenile has a browner throat.

name: Timor Oriole
rangeDescription: Rote, timor, and semau (eastern lesser sundas)
description: Male is a distinctive oriole with a green head, dark mask, and orange-red bill. Duller female is brown above and paler below, with a dark mask and black bill.

name: Elegant Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea
description: A fairly small honeyeater of lowland and foothill wooded habitats. Note the long, slender bill and large yellow ear spot curving around the back of the eye and edged with black.

name: Fiery-billed Aracari
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of costa rica and western panama (western chiriquí)
description: Aracaris are medium-sized toucans, rather slender and long tailed. Fiery-billed is distinctive: the top half of the bill is bright orange.

name: Three-banded Rosefinch
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of western china; winters to southeastern tibet
description: Distinctive and uncommon rosefinch with a long tail. Male is strikingly unmistakable, with grayish “peppery” cheeks, white wing patches, and dark pink crown, back, and breast.

name: Fire-bellied Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Sierra leone and southern guinea to southern nigeria and southwestern cameroon
description: A large, long-billed woodpecker with an olive back, a red rump, a bold facial pattern, and heavily marked underparts with a bright red central belly stripe. The crown and back of the head are black in the female and red in males.

name: Zebra Dove
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar through the thai-malay peninsula to sumatra, java, and lombok; also philippines (native or introduced?), and many feral populations, e.g. the seychelles, mascarenes, indochina, borneo, hawaii, and tahiti, among others
description: A small, grayish brown dove with dark bars on the breast and back, and bare blue skin around the eye. The call is a rapid series of short “coos,” higher pitched and faster than Spotted Dove.
